title: Mitigating fix reversal: Counterfactual constraints for function-level vulnerability detection
abstract: arXiv:2611.24489v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Function-level vulnerability detectors often exhibit fix reversal, assigning a higher vulnerability probability to a fixed version than to its vulnerable counterpart. Fixes usually lengthen functions, and larger length increases are associated with more severe reversal. Code-transformation experiments indicate that fix reversal mainly stems from a length shortcut: vulnerability probability increases with function length when content is fixed. We propose CFVul to address this problem. Sliding-window encoding covers complete functions, retaining fix information beyond the truncation boundary. During training, a content constraint encourages the vulnerable version to receive a higher vulnerability probability under a common length input. During inference, a length constraint averages vulnerability probabilities over fixed reference lengths, reducing the influence of actual length changes. On PrimeVul, CFVul achieves a fix-pair ranking met

translated_title: 缓解修复反转：面向函数级漏洞检测的反事实约束
translated_abstract: 函数级漏洞检测器常常表现出“修复反转”现象，即给修复后的版本赋予比漏洞版本更高的漏洞概率。修复通常会延长函数长度，且长度增加越大，反转现象越严重。代码变换实验表明，修复反转主要源于长度捷径：当内容固定时，漏洞概率随函数长度增加而上升。我们提出CFVul来解决这一问题。滑动窗口编码覆盖完整函数，保留了截断边界之外的修复信息。在训练阶段，内容约束促使漏洞版本在相同长度输入下获得更高的漏洞概率。在推理阶段，长度约束对固定参考长度下的漏洞概率进行平均，降低了实际长度变化的影响。在PrimeVul数据集上，CFVul在修复对排序指标上取得了……
tldr: CFVul通过滑动窗口编码保留完整修复信息，并利用训练时的内容约束和推理时的长度约束等反事实手段，缓解了函数级漏洞检测中因长度捷径导致的“修复反转”问题。
